flashcards.q: What changed when Vertex AI Agent Builder became Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (April 22, 2026)?
flashcards.a: Absorbed Vertex AI Agent Builder + Agentspace into one namespace, inverted console hierarchy (agents first-class, model training/AutoML/Endpoints now sub-features), made A2A v1.0 the default interop layer, added Agent Studio (low-code) + Agent Gateway. Console-level/organizational change -- underlying APIs, SDKs, and billing for existing Vertex AI workloads unchanged. 'Vertex AI' label gone from console as of 2026-05-21.

flashcards.q: How are Vertex AI / Gemini Enterprise prediction endpoints billed, and what's the common cost trap?
flashcards.a: Per hour for every model deployed to an endpoint, regardless of whether it's serving traffic -- you must explicitly undeploy to stop the charge. Common trap: a demo model gets deployed, demo ends, nobody undeploys, endpoint bills 24/7 indefinitely.

flashcards.q: State Gemini 3.1 Pro and 3.5 Flash pricing including the long-context surcharge.
flashcards.a: 3.1 Pro: 2M context, $2.00/$12.00 per 1M input/output tokens under 200K, rising to $2.50/$15.00 above 200K (surcharge applies to the WHOLE call, not just the excess). 3.5 Flash: 1M context, $1.50/$9.00. Flash-Lite: $0.10/$0.40, cheapest tier.

flashcards.q: What cost-saving levers do the Gemini Batch API and context caching offer?
flashcards.a: Batch API: flat 50% discount on any model with a 24-hour processing SLA -- default choice for non-synchronous workloads. Context caching: cuts cost of repeated large-context prompts (shared system prompt, reused document) by up to ~90%, since cached tokens bill at a steep discount vs fresh input tokens.

flashcards.q: What is the Agent Development Kit (ADK) and what are its core primitives?
flashcards.a: Open-source, code-first (Python/Go/Java) agent framework, explicitly model-agnostic and deployment-agnostic (optimized for Gemini, not locked to it). Core primitives: multi-agent hierarchy composition, rich tool ecosystem, graph-based workflow runtime (routing/fan-out/loops/retry/human-in-the-loop), ADK Web (local dev/debug UI with events/traces/artifacts/evals).

flashcards.q: Distinguish Agent Engine's Sessions from Memory Bank.
flashcards.a: Sessions: short-term, persists chronological interaction history within ONE conversation for contextual continuity. Memory Bank (GA early 2026): long-term, extracts salient facts across sessions and stores them for cross-session retrieval. Conflating them causes an agent to 'forget' facts from prior sessions if Memory Bank isn't enabled/populated.

flashcards.q: Contrast Vertex AI Vector Search's brute-force and tree-AH (ANN) index types.
flashcards.a: Brute force: exact linear search, no tunable parameters, appropriate only for small datasets or ground-truth baseline -- latency scales linearly with dataset size, breaks down at scale. Tree-AH/ANN (ScaNN-based): ~99% recall, sub-10ms latency even at billion-vector scale -- the production-appropriate choice. SOAR algorithm adds controlled redundancy for efficiency at smaller index sizes.

flashcards.q: When should you use Vector Search vs AlloyDB AI/Spanner's built-in vector index?
flashcards.a: Vector Search: dedicated, purpose-built for genuine large scale (millions-to-billions of vectors, high QPS) -- bills per-node-hour regardless of traffic, same undeploy trap as prediction endpoints. AlloyDB AI (ScaNN) or Spanner vector index: better when the vector workload can live alongside existing operational data at smaller scale, avoiding a second separately-billed system.

flashcards.q: Distinguish the A2A and MCP protocols.
flashcards.a: MCP (Model Context Protocol): agent-to-TOOL communication -- how an agent calls external tools/data sources. A2A (Agent2Agent): agent-to-AGENT communication -- how one agent hands off tasks to or communicates with another independent agent (task delegation, status, artifacts). Complementary, not substitutes; donated to Linux Foundation June 2025, v1.0 early 2026, 150+ supporting orgs claimed.

flashcards.q: Give the one-line honest positioning of Bedrock AgentCore, Azure AI Foundry, and Gemini Enterprise (ADK+Agent Engine).
flashcards.a: AgentCore: modular composable primitives (Runtime/Memory/Identity/Gateway/Policy), strongest zero-trust/multi-tenant story. Azure AI Foundry: bundled Agent Service, wins decisively for Microsoft 365-native orgs (one-click Teams/Copilot, days not months time-to-value). Gemini Enterprise: code-first ADK + managed Agent Engine, tightest GCP data-platform integration (BigQuery/Vector Search/Spanner), newest rebrand (docs churn risk).

flashcards.q: What is Model Garden and how does third-party model pricing work there?
flashcards.a: Vertex AI/Gemini Enterprise's catalog of 200+ models (Gemini, Claude, Llama, Mistral, Gemma, others) behind one deployment/billing surface. Third-party model pricing is set by the model vendor (e.g. Claude via Model Garden costs roughly what it costs via Bedrock) -- platform choice is rarely about that model's price, more about surrounding tooling fit.

flashcards.q: What changed about the Gemini API free tier on April 1, 2026?
flashcards.a: Free tier now covers only Flash and Flash-Lite models -- Pro-tier models became paid-only. A common gotcha for anyone assuming free-tier prototyping automatically covers the top model.
